scope: Read-only actual saved local AArch64 field decode/accessor audit. Width M255 and M4095; planes, Series, Tuple64, Hybrid32 and Hybrid128.

provenance.qualification: Parent identified saved asm as original final fields cut. Mutable binary and live layout files subsequently changed for paid projection; neither was used. Hardware measurement/source campaign remains parent-owned.

point_calls_per_item.qualification: Same counts at M255/M4095, sequential/shuffled; no cold/helper calls in any selected decode body. Tuple helpers themselves call-free and stack-free. Base is inline even for Tuple64.

findings: All forty selected decode bodies are call-free. No decoded lane array or 64-byte Tuple packet survives; observed decode stack references are only 16/32-byte callee-save areas. Source decode and sum are compiler-visible, with no array escape barrier.

Tuple64 bulk hoists bound plan/view pointers and some control fields before traversal. Each group still tests runtime chunk extents/count/routes and executes native shuffle/shift/mask alternatives. M255 one-byte fields still use prepared routes; M4095 low-byte/high-nibble codes already produce native u16 lanes without per-rank scalar reassembly.

Series M255 body format is identity; local checksum lowering splits native input into scalar byte loads and D-lane extraction. Series M4095 uses fixed 8-byte body plus 4-byte residual tail per eight values, scalar butterfly residual expansion and native widening/OR. No runtime prepared-plan route in Series.

Planes/hybrid group checksums lower to sixteen scalar byte/halfword loads plus scalar add reduction. Tuple64/Series M4095 extract sixteen native u16 lanes and add in scalar registers. Shared no-SLP control does not disable explicit intrinsics or loop vectorization; these are fused decode-plus-sum consumers.

Tuple64 point geometry/used/dead/start remain outlined, with ordinary per-rank prepared GPR controls for selected fields. M4095 used helper0x7d590 selects rank modulo16 using0x68-byte plan stride and branches on slot/transfer controls. Point drivers request only the selected field; no unused aggregate-state collateral remains.

Shuffled ranks are the common computed full-domain permutation, with no query table. Series point M4095 selects one body byte and one shared4-byte residual tail, then fixed extraction; planes/hybrid use selected scalar loads. Tuple point routing is additional to this rank/address work, not intrinsic to the low-byte/high-nibble bits.

Dead bulk controls use the same four-u64 popcounts for planes/Series/hybrid. Planes/Series local compiler vectorizes across eight blocks with CNT/widen/zip accumulation; hybrids retain one-block four-D CNT/ADDV reductions. Tuple64 performs sixteen strided u16 mask popcounts per block. Whole-body counts do not give per-block instruction ratios.

Checkpoint bulk consumes each group base once: planes/hybrid use dense u32 values, Tuple64 uses u32 at64-byte stride, Series fixed16/20-bit formats. Point checkpoint test weights each base sixteen times; bulk ns_per_item denominator is checkpoints, not rows. Physical load reuse may differ from logical requests.

Hybrid32 and Hybrid128 R/U source formulas and local decoder shapes are the same; checkpoint/dead control stride96 versus128 changes physical placement. No intrinsic decoder change is established by any timing difference.

No source fairness blocker found. Concrete routing control if needed: same-format direct unpack of requested TupleGroup lanes, charged same byte bounds/checksum, to separate plan interpretation from format transform. An explicit horizontal checksum control would need symmetric logical sums/overflow semantics.
limits: Static counts include alignment padding and generic alternatives, not executed per item.
Point and bulk consumers differ: point checkpoint repeats group base per row; decode bases consumes each once. Dead bulk is popcount, not materialization.
No SLP shared control still permits loop vectorization and explicit native code; decoded values feed sum without a barrier, so it measures fused decode+sum.

Saved asm source correspondence follows parent-owned final capture and verified captured source hashes; mutable live binary/source were not used. Not native hardware measurement; current compile commands belong to a later rebuild and are not charged to this asm.
